original_question: Suppose that G is a finite group, and A1, A2, A3 are subsets of G such that the multiplication map A1 × A2 × A3 → G is bijective. Must the subgroup ⟨A2 ⟩ generated by A2 have order divisible by the cardinality |A2 |? This is Question 8 in(G. M. Bergman, J. Iranian Math. Soc., 1(2020), 157–161). It is known(ibid.) that the corresponding statement is true for the subgroups ⟨A1 ⟩ and ⟨A3 ⟩. Moreover, |A2 | will at least divide the order of the least subgroup containing A2 and closed under conjugation by members of A1, and similarly of the least subgroup containing A2 and closed under conjugation by members of A3.
target_in_paper: Open problem 21.18 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of arXiv:1401.0300, which the entry itself identifies as Bergman's Question 8 from "A note on factorizations of finite groups."
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's target almost exactly: it quantifies over a finite group G and subsets A1, A2, A3; it uses the bijectivity hypothesis on the multiplication map from A1 × A2 × A3 to G; it asks the precise divisibility question about the order of the subgroup ⟨A2⟩; and it also includes the two contextual remarks recorded alongside the problem, namely the known positive result for ⟨A1⟩ and ⟨A3⟩ and the weaker conjugation-closure divisibility statement for A2.
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, the multiplication map should be written explicitly as (a1,a2,a3) ↦ a1a2a3.
The bibliographic parentheticals should be removed from the question itself; they are provenance, not mathematical content.
The last two sentences in your draft are background results, not additional hypotheses of the open problem, so that should be made explicit in the final formulation.
No extra assumptions such as identity elements lying in the Ai, normality of any Ai, or subgroup conditions on any Ai are part of the question.
This is a pure finite-group factorization problem; ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, and asymptotic phrases such as "for all sufficiently large" are not applicable here.
refined_question: Let G be a finite group, and let A1, A2, A3 be subsets of G such that the map A1 × A2 × A3 → G given by (a1,a2,a3) ↦ a1a2a3 is bijective. Must the subgroup ⟨A2⟩ generated by A2 have order divisible by |A2|?
justification: The nearest official formulation in arXiv:1401.0300 is Problem 21.18, and your draft is essentially a verbatim restatement of that entry. The bijective-product setup is the formulation used in Bergman's note, where Question 8 is stated in the same 3-factor form. The contextual statements you included are also paper-faithful: the endpoint analogues for ⟨A1⟩ and ⟨A3⟩ come from the divisibility result for outer factors (Lemma 2), while the weaker middle-factor divisibility via conjugation-closed subgroups is the content immediately leading up to Question 8 (Lemma 7). So the only real sharpening needed is to make the map explicit and separate the core open question from its surrounding background.
